pages.text: Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee lived in the ocean. All day long she clung to the same slippery rock with her single big foot. Her tiny tentacles caught tasty treats.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: We meet a sea anemone fixed to one rock, feeding with her tentacles.

illustration.only_in_image: Her face is smiling and content; she is pink on a large brown-green rock.

pages.text: On days when she felt cross, her stinging tentacles kept the other creatures away.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Her stinging tentacles show she can push others away when cross.

illustration.only_in_image: Her frowning eyes and one long tentacle swatting toward fish who swim off.

pages.text: But today her rock felt lonely.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Today the rock feels lonely: the want for company is named.

illustration.only_in_image: She is tiny in a crowded reef full of other creatures moving about, which makes the loneliness visible.

pages.text:
“I have no fins.
I have no feet.
I am different to every other creature.”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She lists what she lacks and feels different from every creature.

illustration.only_in_image: Each creature with fins or feet is placed beside the matching line; her face is sad.

pages.text:
“Even that hermit crab is off having adventures!”
“Save me! That fish wants to pluck me out of my shell!”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She envies the crab's adventures; then the crab cries for help from a fish.

illustration.only_in_image: A toothy fish's mouth enters at the top corner: the threat appears in the picture before the text names it fully.

pages.text:
Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee whipped up her stinging tentacles and hid the hermit underneath them.
“Go away, you big bully!”
The big fish bared his teeth, but was afraid of being stung.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She uses her stings to shelter the crab and faces the big fish down.

pages.text:
He gave up and swam away with a cheeky flick of his tail.
“That was close!” said the crab. “Is it safe now?”
“You can come out, Crab. What’s your name?”
“Herman. I’m a hermit, but I think I need a bodyguard. I wish I was as brave as you!”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: The fish leaves; the crab, Herman, wishes he were as brave as her.

illustration.only_in_image: Her face stays grumpy while the crab snuggles in; only the fish's tail remains.

pages.text:
“I’m Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee. I wish I had amazing adventures like you.”
“But why don’t you?” He asked.
“I’m stuck to my rock. And I don’t have legs!” She replied.
“Well, I don’t have stings, but I do have an idea!”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She confides her wish and her limits; Herman says he has an idea.

repetition.note: I don't have ... mirrors her earlier list

pages.text:
Herman took Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee by the tentacle and danced around her, pulling silly faces.
First Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee snorted, and then she giggled — and then she laughed so hard she popped right off her rock.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Herman makes her laugh so hard she pops off her rock.

illustration.only_in_image: She floats free in mid-water, eyes shut laughing.

pages.text:
Herman gently picked her up and settled her on his shell.
“Are you ready? I feel an adventure coming on.” He said.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Herman settles her on his shell; they set off together.

illustration.only_in_image: White background; the two are now one shape, anemone sitting atop the shell.

pages.text:
Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee adventures all over the ocean, catching tasty treats.
Now she only uses her stinging tentacles to keep the nasty fish away from Herman.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She travels the ocean and now guards Herman: the stings have a new purpose.

repetition.note: tasty treats and stinging tentacles from the opening

illustration.only_in_image: Bubble vignettes show places she visits: fish school, eel in kelp, turtle, octopus.

pages.text: And she never, ever feels lonely.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She is never lonely again: the opening want is answered.
